disclaimer: If you think you react to this, ask an allergist; reactions to additives are hard to prove and are rarely confirmed in tests.

additives.rarity: Affects an estimated 3% to 10% of individuals with asthma; under 0.1% in the general non-asthmatic population.
additives.description: Sulfites are widespread preservatives that can trigger sudden wheezing or tightness in the chest, primarily in people who have asthma.
additives.asthma_note: Sulfites are the additive most often linked to breathing symptoms in people with asthma.

sources.citation: Skypala et al. Clin Transl Allergy 2015; 5:34
Journal of Food Allergy 2021; Adverse reactions to food additives

relevant_groups: individuals with house dust mite or crustacean (shrimp) allergy
additives.rarity: Documented cause of true IgE-mediated food allergy; about 3% of patients with suspected additive symptoms were sensitized in clinical studies.
additives.description: Carmine is a natural crimson red colour extracted from insects that can cause genuine allergic reactions including hives, facial swelling, or anaphylaxis.

sources.citation: Allergo Journal International 2022; Anaphylaxis to food additives
Journal of Food Allergy 2021; Adverse reactions to food additives

relevant_groups: people with asthma or sulfite sensitivity
additives.rarity: Contains residual bound and free sulfites that can trigger symptoms in sensitive asthmatics.
additives.description: Sulfite caramel colours are brown colorings manufactured with sulfites, which can release residual sulfites and trigger wheezing in asthmatics.
additives.asthma_note: Contains residual sulfites, which are the additive most often linked to breathing symptoms in people with asthma.

sources.citation: Skypala et al. Clin Transl Allergy 2015

relevant_groups: children and adults with idiopathic hives or swelling
additives.rarity: Rare cause of IgE reactions, but one of the natural colours most frequently confirmed in anaphylaxis workups.
additives.description: Annatto is a yellow-orange plant extract used in cheeses and snacks that has been confirmed in rare cases to trigger hives or anaphylaxis.

sources.citation: Journal of Food Allergy 2021; Adverse reactions to food additives
Allergo Journal International 2022; Anaphylaxis to food additives

additives.rarity: A few isolated clinical case reports of contact hives, asthma, and rare anaphylaxis.
additives.description: Guar gum is a natural thickening agent made from legume seeds that has caused rare confirmed cases of anaphylaxis, especially in people with legume allergies.

additives.rarity: Well-known occupational inhalant allergen; dietary systemic reactions are exceptionally rare.
additives.description: Gum arabic is a tree sap stabilizer that is a recognized occupational allergen and has caused isolated case reports of food-triggered allergic reactions.

additives.rarity: Scattered medical case reports in infants and legume-sensitized patients.
additives.description: Locust bean gum is a thickening agent milled from carob seeds that can rarely cause allergic reactions or infant feeding intolerance.

relevant_groups: patients with red meat / alpha-gal allergy
additives.rarity: A small series of documented life-threatening anaphylaxis cases confirmed via skin and IgE tests.
additives.description: Carrageenan is a seaweed extract used to thicken puddings and dairy that has been documented in rare case reports to cause severe anaphylaxis.

relevant_groups: consumers of diet drinks and thickeners
additives.rarity: Repeatedly identified as a hidden cause in severe unexplained anaphylaxis workups.
additives.description: Carboxymethylcellulose is a modified cellulose thickener that is an established, though rare, hidden trigger of severe allergic anaphylaxis.

relevant_groups: individuals allergic to cashew nut or pistachio
additives.rarity: Isolated clinical reports of severe IgE anaphylaxis; cross-reacts with cashew and pistachio.
additives.description: Pectin is a natural fruit gelling agent that can rarely provoke anaphylaxis, particularly in people with cashew or pistachio allergies.

additives.rarity: Well-known occupational allergen with scattered case reports of severe dietary anaphylaxis.
additives.description: Gum tragacanth is a legume-derived plant resin that has been linked to rare but severe allergic reactions and anaphylaxis.

relevant_groups: consumers of keto, sugar-free, or zero-calorie foods
additives.rarity: Multiple published clinical case reports confirm immediate IgE-mediated urticaria and anaphylaxis.
additives.description: Erythritol is a zero-calorie sugar alcohol that has been documented in multiple clinical reports to cause immediate allergic hives and anaphylaxis.

relevant_groups: patients reacting to chewable tablets, mints, or diet foods
additives.rarity: Extremely rare; confirmed in isolated case reports as an IgE-mediated trigger.
additives.description: Mannitol is a sugar alcohol sweetener with rare but confirmed clinical case reports of life-threatening allergic reactions.

relevant_groups: healthcare workers/caregivers who handle laxative powders
additives.rarity: Established cause of severe anaphylaxis after prior inhalation or occupational sensitisation.
additives.description: Psyllium husk is a natural plant fiber that can cause severe anaphylaxis, especially in people previously sensitised through handling fiber powders.

relevant_groups: patients reacting to commercial dressings/ice creams
additives.rarity: Recognized cause of excipient-induced anaphylaxis; food-borne reactions are rare but verified.
additives.description: Polysorbate 80 is an emulsifier that has been verified in medical case reports to cause rare but severe allergic anaphylaxis.

relevant_groups: individuals allergic to bell peppers, chili, or nightshades
additives.rarity: Infrequent cause of food allergy; reactions occur mostly in individuals cross-sensitised to Capsicum.
additives.description: Paprika extract is a natural red-orange colouring from sweet peppers that can provoke allergic reactions in individuals allergic to peppers.

relevant_groups: individuals cross-reactive to olive or mugwort pollen
additives.rarity: Rare cause of severe food allergy; verified by skin prick and basophil activation tests.
additives.description: Saffron is an expensive natural spice and colour that has been documented in rare case reports to cause IgE-mediated anaphylaxis.

relevant_groups: individuals with contact allergy to insect resins
additives.rarity: Recognized cause of contact cheilitis; severe immediate systemic food reactions are exceedingly rare.
additives.description: Shellac is an insect-derived glossy glaze on candies and pills that can occasionally trigger lip swelling, mouth irritation, or hives.

additives.rarity: Documented in medical case reports as a cause of severe anaphylactoid reactions; dietary reactions are exceedingly rare.
additives.description: Indigo Carmine is a deep blue synthetic dye known in medical literature to cause rare, severe allergic-like reactions with low blood pressure.

additives.rarity: Well-known cause of anaphylaxis in clinical lymph node procedures; oral food cases are exceptionally rare.
additives.description: Patent Blue V is a synthetic blue colour that has documented case reports of severe allergic reactions and anaphylaxis.

relevant_groups: individuals with chronic urticaria or aspirin-sensitive asthma reporting sensitivities
additives.rarity: Double-blind placebo-controlled trials have consistently found reactions in fewer than 1% of suspected patients; widely perceived sensitivities are rarely test-confirmed.
additives.description: Tartrazine is a bright yellow synthetic dye that was historically blamed for asthma and hives, though rigorous blinded medical trials have not confirmed this link.
additives.weak_evidence_note: Blinded placebo-controlled challenge tests have not confirmed that tartrazine triggers asthma or hives.

sources.citation: Journal of Food Allergy 2021; Adverse reactions to food additives

additives.rarity: Controlled challenge studies have rarely confirmed reactions; immunologic mechanisms have not been established.
additives.description: Sunset Yellow is an orange-yellow synthetic food dye occasionally suspected of causing hives, but controlled allergy testing has not confirmed a link.
additives.weak_evidence_note: Blinded placebo-controlled tests have not confirmed an allergic mechanism for Sunset Yellow.

relevant_groups: people reporting sensitivities to synthetic dyes
additives.rarity: Extremely rare anecdotal reports; blinded trials show no reproducible allergic reactions above placebo.
additives.description: Allura Red is a common red synthetic dye that has been blamed for hives in personal reports, but placebo-controlled studies have not demonstrated allergic reactions.
additives.weak_evidence_note: Blinded tests have not substantiated allergic reactions to Allura Red.

additives.rarity: Documented allergic reactions are virtually non-existent in clinical literature.
additives.description: Brilliant Blue is a synthetic food colouring with an exceptionally safe record, where reported skin reactions remain unconfirmed in clinical testing.
additives.weak_evidence_note: Blinded studies have not confirmed allergic reactions to Brilliant Blue.

relevant_groups: patients with chronic spontaneous urticaria or nasal polyps
additives.rarity: True adverse reactions are proven in under 1-2% of tested individuals with chronic urticaria, and are virtually absent in the general population.
additives.description: Sodium benzoate is a common preservative widely blamed for hives and asthma, but blinded hospital challenges rarely confirm a true reaction.
additives.weak_evidence_note: Well-designed blinded clinical trials have not confirmed that sodium benzoate causes allergic hives or asthma.

sources.citation: Skypala et al. Clin Transl Allergy 2015

additives.rarity: Oral systemic allergic reactions are extremely rare and lack confirmation in controlled challenges.
additives.description: Potassium sorbate is an antifungal preservative that can irritate the skin directly, but rarely or never causes internal allergic reactions.
additives.weak_evidence_note: Oral systemic allergy to sorbates has not been confirmed in controlled testing.

sources.citation: Skypala et al. Clin Transl Allergy 2015

reactions: sweating (historical complaints; not reproducible under blinded challenge)
additives.rarity: Placebo-controlled double-blind trials consistently show that adverse reactions to MSG do not exceed placebo rates.
additives.description: Monosodium glutamate is a savory flavour enhancer widely accused of causing headaches and flushing, but controlled blinded trials have found no reproducible allergy.
additives.weak_evidence_note: Rigorous double-blind placebo-controlled trials have consistently shown that MSG does not cause reproducible allergic reactions.

sources.citation: Skypala et al. Clin Transl Allergy 2015

additives.rarity: Multiple rigorous double-blind challenges have failed to verify any immunologic or reproducible intolerance.
additives.description: Aspartame is an artificial sweetener commonly suspected of triggering headaches and hives, though blinded clinical trials show no more reactions than a dummy pill.
additives.weak_evidence_note: Blinded challenge studies in people reporting hives after aspartame found no more reactions than with a placebo.

reactions: dermatitis (historical reports; unconfirmed in blinded challenges)
additives.rarity: Extremely weak evidence base; almost never confirmed in blinded oral challenges.
additives.description: BHA and BHT are synthetic antioxidants that preserve fats, with historical claims of worsening hives that modern allergy testing has failed to verify.
additives.weak_evidence_note: A link between BHA/BHT and chronic hives has not been verified in controlled challenge studies.

sources.citation: Skypala et al. Clin Transl Allergy 2015

additives.rarity: Aside from rare vascular flushing or isolated case reports, convincing evidence for an allergic reaction is absent.
additives.description: Nitrites and nitrates are meat-curing salts that can cause mild facial flushing or headaches from blood vessel dilation, but do not cause true food allergies.
additives.weak_evidence_note: No convincing scientific evidence demonstrates an allergic mechanism for nitrites or nitrates.

sources.citation: Skypala et al. Clin Transl Allergy 2015

relevant_groups: individuals with contact allergy to cosmetics or lip balms
additives.rarity: Oral systemic reactions have not been demonstrated in clinical trials.
additives.description: Propyl gallate and TBHQ are oil antioxidants that can cause contact skin rash, but have not been proven to cause internal food allergies.
additives.weak_evidence_note: Oral dietary reactions have not been confirmed in controlled allergy testing.

sources.citation: Skypala et al. Clin Transl Allergy 2015

relevant_groups: individuals with contact allergy to spices
additives.rarity: Contact allergy is known, but ingestion-related allergic reactions are practically unknown in clinical challenge studies.
additives.description: Curcumin is the yellow pigment from turmeric that can irritate the skin upon direct contact, but rarely causes allergic problems when eaten.
additives.weak_evidence_note: Allergic reactions to swallowed curcumin are not supported by blinded medical evidence.

additives.rarity: Allergic reactions are practically non-existent in clinical literature.
additives.description: Plain and ammonia caramel colourings are heated sugar products that do not contain sulfites and have an established record of allergy safety.
additives.weak_evidence_note: No immunologic allergic mechanism has been established for plain or ammonia caramel colours.

relevant_groups: individuals with allergic contact dermatitis from cosmetics
additives.rarity: Contact dermatitis is common, but oral dietary allergy is rarely proven in controlled medical tests.
additives.description: Parabens are antimicrobial preservatives that can cause topical skin rashes, but do not reliably produce food allergy reactions when swallowed.
additives.weak_evidence_note: Oral challenge studies have failed to demonstrate reproducible food allergic reactions to parabens.
